CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for infection concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury who presents for follow-up after recent hospitalization (admitted 06/29/2021, discharged 07/02/2021). During hospitalization, she presented with spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department, she was febrile with WBC of 23,000. She was treated with IV antibiotic therapy for concerns of urinary tract infection and developed labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Patient attributes her presentation primarily to constipation and autonomic dysreflexia rather than urinary tract infection. She notes she did not have regular bowel movements during hospitalization but felt significantly better after discharge once she had a substantial bowel movement. She states the weather was extremely hot during the period leading to hospitalization. Currently reports feeling back to normal and denies pain or discomfort. She has a suprapubic catheter. She manages constipation with miralax daily, doubling the dose when needed, though reports frequently going extended periods without regular bowel movements despite this regimen. Urine cultures obtained during hospitalization were not impressive. Doctor noted her white count was normal last year, suggesting recent elevation may be related to inflammation from constipation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain or discomfort.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax (daily, doubled when needed)
Lactulose (for severe constipation)
Vitamin C
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is unvaccinated for COVID-19. She is hesitant regarding the vaccine due to concerns about unknown side effects and reports of vaccine injury. She does not receive annual flu shots. She takes vitamin C and multivitamins. She is closely monitored. She tends to stay indoors more during hot weather. She is somewhat homeopathic in her approach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lung auscultation performed with patient instructed to take deep breaths and breathe normally. Denies pain or discomfort on examination.

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization:
- WBC: 23,000 (elevated)
- Urine cultures: not impressive
- X-rays obtained
- Historical WBC: normal last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to chronic constipation: Patient attributes recent hospitalization to constipation and autonomic dysreflexia from quadriplegia with significant vital sign changes rather than true urinary tract infection. She maintains good bowel regimen with miralax daily and lactulose for severe constipation. Plan: Follow-up in 2-3 weeks for fasting labs including CBC and cholesterol panel to recheck white blood cell count to ensure downward trend.

2. Quadriplegia: Stable. Discussed that autonomic dysreflexia typically does not affect white blood cell count.

3. COVID-19 vaccine status: Patient is currently unvaccinated and hesitant regarding vaccine due to concerns about unknown side effects and vaccine injury reports. Does not receive annual flu shots. Doctor recommended vaccination as the only true preventative mechanism for COVID-19 and discussed that supplements would not provide adequate protection. Doctor noted patient is at high risk based on quadriplegia status. Patient is open-minded but not ready to proceed with vaccination at this time.
